q1: False. HTML is a markup language, not a programming language. It describes structure and meaning but has no logic, loops, or conditionals.
q2: C - Structuring content and giving it semantic meaning. HTML's job is structure and semantics; CSS handles styling (A), JavaScript handles interactivity (B), and HTML doesn't compile to machine code (D).
q3: WHATWG (Web Hypertext Application Technology Working Group). The WHATWG maintains the HTML Living Standard as a continuously evolving specification.
q4: Browser sends request → Server responds with HTML → Browser parses HTML and builds DOM → Browser paints page. This is the correct order of the request-render cycle.
q5: WHATWG. The Web Hypertext Application Technology Working Group maintains the HTML Living Standard as a continuously evolving specification.
q6: Structuring content and giving it meaning. HTML's main job is structure and semantics, not styling (CSS) or interactivity (JavaScript).
q7: Hyper Text Markup Language. HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language.
q8: Adding complex interactivity and logic. HTML's three main responsibilities are: giving text meaning (semantics), structuring documents, and embedding content. Interactivity is JavaScript's job.
q9: An in-memory tree representation of the HTML. The DOM is the browser's live in-memory tree built from HTML source, not the original file itself.
q10: False. HTML describes structure and meaning, not visual appearance. Styling is handled by CSS.
